fluff.overview: The Star League Defense Force's drive toward military specialization across all domains of warfare led to the development of numerous purpose-built combat platforms during the twenty-seventh century. Among these was the Manta Fast Attack Submarine, designed in 2698 by the Royal Nelson Memorial Shipwrights of Portsmouth on Terra. Commissioned for the SLDF's elite Royal CAAN (Combined Armor, Air, and Naval) regiments, the fifty-ton Manta filled a critical niche as a rapid-response undersea interceptor. Built on a hull optimized for raw speed, the submarine was intended to operate in tandem with the larger Moray Heavy Attack Submarine. Where the Moray provided heavy firepower and endurance, the Manta brought unmatched underwater agility to the pairing. The design earned a reputation as one of the fastest military submarines ever fielded, though its lightweight construction and minimal armament made it dependent on its heavier companion for sustained engagements.
fluff.capabilities:
The Manta's design philosophy prioritized speed above all other considerations. Its GM 320 XL fusion engine consumes nearly eighteen tons of the submarine's fifty-ton displacement, granting a remarkable underwater flank speed of 119 kilometers per hour. This extreme power-to-weight ratio comes at significant cost, however. The oversized powerplant leaves little internal volume for weapons or protection, forcing designers to accept severe compromises in both areas.

Nine tons of AmberStar Weave ferro-fibrous armor protect the hull, concentrated heavily in the bow to support the Manta's preferred attack profile of high-speed nose-on passes. Coverage along the flanks and stern is particularly thinner, leaving the vessel vulnerable if forced into a turning engagement. The armor distribution reflects a tactical doctrine built around slashing attacks rather than prolonged exchanges of fire.

Armament is limited to a single Selitex Aqua extended-range large laser and a Sea Harvester six-tube short-range torpedo launcher mounted in the nose. The torpedo launcher carries only a single ton of ammunition, restricting the Manta to brief engagements before needing to withdraw and rearm. While the laser provides unlimited firepower for repeated passes, the overall weapons load is light for a fifty-ton platform.
fluff.deployment: The baseline Manta remains the primary fast attack variant in Republic of the Sphere service. Originally fielded by the SLDF in 2698, the design was reintroduced by the Word of Blake during the Jihad with no significant modifications to its original configuration. Republic Naval Command continues to deploy the standard Manta in its traditional escort role alongside Moray submarines, providing rapid-response capability for underwater task forces. The type also serves in independent patrol and reconnaissance missions where its exceptional speed allows it to cover vast stretches of ocean quickly.
fluff.history:
The Manta entered service with the SLDF's Royal CAAN regiments in 2698, deployed extensively across the Terran Hegemony's ocean worlds. The submarines proved their worth during the Amaris Coup, participating in resistance operations against the Usurper's occupation forces on Terra and other Hegemony worlds. Both the Manta and its Moray partner suffered heavy losses during the protracted liberation campaign, and surviving hulls were scattered across Hegemony worlds with little prospect of replacement.

The Succession Wars completed the Manta's decline. Without the advanced manufacturing capability needed to maintain the design's extra-light fusion engine and ferro-fibrous armor, operational examples dwindled to extinction across the Inner Sphere. ComStar eventually located surviving hulls on Terra and quietly decommissioned them, adding the submarines to its vast stockpile of preserved Star League technology.

Centuries later, the Word of Blake inherited these reserves when it seized control of Terra. As part of its broader reactivation program, the Word commissioned Royal Nelson's dormant shipyard in Portsmouth to restart Manta production. The new submarines were assigned to escort the massive Wyrm SDS Submersible Fortresses, providing screening and pursuit capability for the mobile underwater weapons platforms. Production runs remained limited, focused primarily on supporting the Wyrm mobile structures, and many of the new-build Mantas were damaged or destroyed during the liberation of Terra in 3079.

Following the Jihad, the Allied Coalition pressed captured Mantas into service hunting rogue Wyrm fortresses still operating under Blakist control. The Republic of the Sphere subsequently retained the design, commissioning further production to support its own re-commissioned Wyrms and to provide undersea security for underwater command installations throughout Republic space.
